method: The chart is a fixed conversion table, not a calculation from the number: each row pairs one shaft diameter in millimetres with its US knitting number, its old UK knitting number (where one exists) and its US crochet hook label (where one exists). Diameters run from 2 mm to 25 mm in 23 rows, and the 14 crochet hooks from B/1 at 2.25 mm to N/15 at 10 mm all sit on the same diameter series, so a hook and a needle that share a millimetre value share a row. Sizes with no number in a system are reported as having none rather than being guessed: 3 mm has no US number, 3.5 mm and 12 mm and above have no old UK number. Input is accepted as a metric value with at most two decimals, a US number with an optional half, an old UK number including 0, 00 and 000, or a hook label with or without its number, so H, H/8 and h-8 all resolve. A value outside 2 to 25 mm, a number that is not in the table, or a blank field is refused with a field-specific message rather than being rounded silently. A metric value that lies between two rows reports the nearest standard size below and above it together with each gap in millimetres, and never interpolates a size that is not manufactured. US and old UK numbers run in opposite directions and were never fully standardised, so the table follows the published Craft Yarn Council and Vogue Knitting conversions and states the millimetre value as the authoritative one; makers disagree at the thick end, where US 17 is sold as 12 mm or 12.75 mm. The tool converts sizes only and gives no gauge, yarn-substitution or tension advice. Everything runs in the browser with no storage, uploads or network access.
